I am old now, 72 years, and I farm my small piece here in Mtwara with my own hands. The cashew is what we know here, and I do not have money for fertilizer or sprays — the rains will come as they come, and I plant my nuts together with cassava as my mother taught me. My grandchildren help me sometimes when school is finished, but my back is not strong like before, so the work is slow.
